meta.title: ai-usagebar: AI plan usage in your top bar
meta.description: ai-usagebar shows quota, balance and reset times for Claude, Codex, Copilot, Z.AI, OpenRouter and 19 more AI providers in Waybar, Omarchy, GNOME, KDE, macOS and Windows.

hero.title: Know how much AI you have left, before it runs out
hero.lede: ai-usagebar reads each plan's usage from the provider and shows it where you already look: the top bar, a terminal UI or the system tray. It began as a Rust port of claudebar and now covers 24 providers.
hero.shotAlt: The ai-usagebar panel open under the Omarchy top bar: Z.AI GLM Coding Pro with session, weekly and monthly MCP quotas at 1%, their reset times, and tabs for Claude, Codex, Z.AI, OpenRouter and Kimi.

why.title: Why I built it
why.lede: I pay for several coding plans and each one meters differently: a 5-hour window here, a weekly cap there, a prepaid balance somewhere else. Opening five dashboards to decide which agent gets the next task was silly. Now one glance at the bar tells me.
why.alt: Seven provider chips, Claude, Codex, Copilot, Z.AI, OpenRouter, Kimi and DeepSeek, feed one bar with a gauge. The zoomed panel shows three meters, the first nearly full with a red marker labelled Alert at 97%, and a Resets in clock.

surfaces.title: Wherever you work
surfaces.lede: The same Rust core feeds every front end, so the numbers match everywhere.

items.title: Terminal UI
items.text: ai-usagebar-tui: a tab per provider, refreshed every 60 seconds, with a settings overlay.
items.alt: The ai-usagebar TUI on the OpenAI tab: Codex 5-hour window at 6% and weekly at 1%, with reset times and pace, and a credits section.

items.title: macOS menu bar
items.text: A native popover with every enabled provider, pace markers and reset times.
items.alt: The macOS tray popover listing Claude Max, Codex, Cursor, SuperGrok and Antigravity, each with usage bars, percentage used and reset times.

items.title: Windows tray
items.text: A notification-area icon with a WebView2 popover. Installs with Scoop.
items.alt: The Windows tray dashboard with provider usage bars.

items.title: KDE Plasma 6
items.text: A plasmoid with provider tabs. Each applet instance can follow a different provider.
items.alt: The KDE Plasma 6 plasmoid showing provider tabs and usage bars.

items.title: Alerts before the wall
items.text: A desktop notification when a quota window crosses 97%, a critical one at 100%, and a warning 48 hours before banked reset credits expire. The threshold is yours to change.

items.title: Finds your accounts
items.text: ai-usagebar detect turns on every provider that already has a credential on the machine. It reads local files and keychains, never the network.

items.title: Keeps showing the last good number
items.text: Network failures keep the previous data on screen. A provider that answers HTTP 429 is left alone for five minutes.

items.title: Several accounts
items.text: Named Claude, Codex and OpenRouter accounts side by side, each with its own entry.

items.title: Drop-in for claudebar
items.text: Same Waybar JSON, flags, Pango tooltip, Omarchy theme detection and locked OAuth refresh.

items.title: Scriptable
items.text: ai-usagebar usage --json prints every provider's quota and reset time as one document.

providers.title: 24 providers
providers.lede: The command line and the TUI support all of them. Desktop coverage varies by integration; the README has the table.
